plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram to assess cardiac function; Initiate diuretic therapy (e.g., furosemide) for volume overload; Monitor for signs and symptoms of worsening heart failure
plan2: Complete iron studies (ferritin, iron saturation) to assess iron deficiency; Consider oral iron supplementation if indicated; Evaluate for chronic blood loss (gastrointestinal source)
plan3: Assess bone density (DEXA scan) for definitive diagnosis; Recommend calcium and vitamin D supplementation; Review medication regimen for osteoporosis treatment (e.g., continue alendronic acid)

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Repeat pulse oximetry within 24 hours; Administer oxygen via nebulizer as needed; Consider hospital admission for further evaluation and management
plan2: Continue as prescribed with metoprolol succinate 100 mg extended release oral tablet, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg/actuat mucosal spray, and simvastatin 20 mg oral tablet; Follow-up with cardiology service within 2 weeks; Order repeat diagnostic imaging of heart and coronary circulation
plan3: Refer to hematologist for evaluation and management; Order complete blood count (CBC) to confirm diagnosis; Consider iron supplementation or other treatments as deemed necessary

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Pursue serial BNP/NT-proBNP to confirm HF progression; assess fluid status with orthostatic BP/HR and ankle edema response.; Consider short-acting nitroglycerin trial if orthopnea persists, followed by diuretic taper (e.g., intravenous furosemide) under monitoring.; Recheck diuretics (potassium/sodium intake review) and optimize MRA use if on ARB/ACE with persistent symptoms.
plan2: Review med adherence (metoprolol/clopidogrel) via phone/multimedia; monitor for CVA/TIA triggers (e.g., orthostatic syncope, nitroglycerin dizziness).; Arrange repeat 12-lead ECG/Echocardiogram within 3 months to evaluate HF stability/LVEF changes post-PCI.; Suggest annual lipid/stress test evaluation if triglycerides/HDL remain suboptimal under current regimen (>165 or <50 mg/dL).
plan3: Review GAD-7 and PHQ-2 results for depressive symptoms; consider referral to mental-health team for anxiety/depression screening.

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Obtain echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction; Check BNP levels to evaluate heart failure severity; Initiate diuretics for fluid management if indicated
plan2: Order spirometry to assess airflow limitation; Consider chest X-ray to rule out other causes of dyspnea; Evaluate for possible rehabilitation therapy
plan3: Check CBC for hemoglobin and hematocrit levels; Consider iron supplementation if deficiency is confirmed; Monitor for symptoms of anemia and adjust management accordingly

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction; BNP level assessment; Assess for edema and orthopnea symptoms
plan2: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential; Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin); Evaluate for chronic kidney disease or medication-induced anemia
plan3: Monitor blood glucose levels; Continue current medication regimen (metoprolol, clopidogrel, simvastatin); Encourage adherence to cardiac rehabilitation program

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Medication review and reassessment of current medications including diuretics and ACE inhibitors; Echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction and BNP levels; Follow-up assessment of orthopnea, edema, and dyspnea
plan2: Spirometry to assess airflow limitation; Chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia or heart failure; Consider referral to pulmonology service
plan3: CBC to evaluate hemoglobin levels and iron deficiency status; Iron supplementation (oral or intravenous) if iron deficiency is confirmed; Follow-up assessment of fatigue and dyspnea

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: obtain BNP level to assess for heart failure severity; chest x-ray to confirm findings or exclude complications; consider echocardiogram to check for ejection fraction
plan2: repeat CBC to check for iron deficiency and assess MCV/MCH to direct ferritin/Transferrin saturation; treat chronic predisposing causes (consider GI evaluation if severe/malabsorption suspect); consider B12/folate if deficiencies suspected and symptomatic

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Order echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction; Check BNP levels to evaluate heart failure severity; Adjust medication regimen for heart failure management
plan2: Schedule spirometry to assess airflow limitation; Consider referral to pulmonary rehabilitation; Review smoking cessation support
plan3: Evaluate iron status with ferritin and iron studies; Consider iron supplementation if iron deficiency is confirmed; Monitor hemoglobin levels regularly

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Order Echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction and valve function; Check BNP levels to assess heart failure severity; Assess for edema and rales
plan2: Complete Blood Count (CBC) to assess hemoglobin levels; Iron studies to determine iron deficiency status; Consider Vitamin B12 or Folate supplementation if deficiency identified
plan3: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate; Continue current medications (Metoprolol, Clopidogrel, Simvastatin, Nitroglycerin); Review coronary angiography report and PCI details

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Invest in echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction; Assess BNP levels to evaluate heart failure severity; Monitor and adjust medications
plan2: Evaluate hemoglobin levels with Complete Blood Count (CBC); Consider iron supplementation or Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) for treatment; Monitor and adjust oxygen therapy as needed
plan3: Schedule spirometry to assess airflow limitation; Discuss smoking cessation resources and support; Consider chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia or heart failure

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Repeat cardiac biomarkers (BNP/NT-proBNP) to assess CHF exacerbation; assess orthopnea/paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea severity further with patient diaries; initiate diuretic optimization (e.g., loop diuretic loading, titrate as tolerated).
diagnosis2: severe ischaemic heart disease with persistent symptoms despite IHD optimization
plan2: Confirm stability on current beta-blocker/antihypertensive therapy; recommend stress echocardiography/DOTA-30 to evaluate residual ischaemia; discuss revascularization plan in 3–6 months per PCI history (e.g., delayed percutaneous angioplasty, CRT-D).
plan3: Draw ferritin/triglyceride-iron complex to differentiate iron/non-iron deficiency anemia; evaluate hematocrit fluctuations or need for ESA/transfusion if haemoglobin <8.0 g/dL; monitor ferritin 80–300 μg/L with low transferrin saturation <20%.

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Adjust diuretics to manage edema and dyspnea; Evaluate current heart medications for optimization; Schedule echocardiogram to assess heart function
plan2: Consider referral to ENT specialist; Assess need for imaging studies (CT scan of sinuses); Review/update sinusitis management plan
plan3: Monitor cardiac symptoms and adjust medications as needed; Perform exercise tolerance testing; Evaluate cardiovascular risk factors including lipid levels

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction and valve function; Initiate or optimize diuretic therapy (e.g., furosemide) to manage edema and dyspnea; Continuous cardiac monitoring and symptom assessment
plan2: Review current cardiac medications and adherence; Consider cardiac rehabilitation program referral; Monitor for any signs of angina or unstable symptoms
plan3: Assess for bacterial sinus infection with culture and antibiotic consideration; Evaluate for nasal obstruction and consider nasal steroid sprays; Discuss patient education on sinusitis management and trigger avoidance

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram to assess pericardial thickness & morphology; Cardiac MRI with contrast to evaluate pericardial abnormalities; Initiate beta-blocker therapy to reduce pericardial stiffness
plan2: Repeat lipid panel to assess progression of dyslipidemia; Perform stress test to evaluate coronary artery flow & ischemia; Initiate dual-antiplatelet therapy with aspirin & P2Y12 inhibitor

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: Heart Failure with preserved EF (HFpEF/diastolic dysfunction)
plan1: Confirm with echocardiogram (EF assessment), assess fluid overload/responses to diuretic therapy; consider repeat BNP/NT-proBNP; monitor for symptoms progression.
plan2: Assess FEV1/FVC ratio on spirometry, monitor home nebulizer effectiveness; evaluate for infection triggers (e.g., sinusitis); screen for adherence to inhaled therapy.
diagnosis3: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) with valvular disease (e.g., aortic valve disease)
plan3: Cardiac imaging echo for structural heart assessment; rule out valvular lesions via Doppler; reassess HF therapy overlap with valvular guidance.

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: initiate diuretics to manage fluid overload; evaluate cardiac function with echocardiogram; optimize heart failure medications and monitor
plan2: perform pulmonary function testing; review nebulizer use and inhaler technique; consider long-acting bronchodilator therapy
plan3: schedule cardiac stress testing; review and optimize current cardiovascular medication regimen; manage risk factors including weight and cholesterol levels

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Initiate diuretic therapy (e.g., furosemide) 20-40 mg IV or PO; Assess ejection fraction with echocardiogram; Monitor closely for signs of worsening heart failure (e.g., shortness of breath, edema)
plan2: Continue current antihypertensive regimen (valsartan, bisoprolol, aspirin, atorvastatin); Consider a stress test to assess prognosis and guide further management; Educate patient on cardiac rehabilitation and lifestyle modifications
plan3: Consider nasal corticosteroids for symptom control; Evaluate for potential fungal or bacterial infection with nasal swab; Consider referral to ENT specialist for further evaluation and potential sinus surgery

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram to assess left ventricular function; Initiate beta-blocker as needed based on clinical assessment; Monitor cardiac output and blood pressure closely for signs of worsening heart failure
plan2: Add topical corticosteroids to existing treatment regimen; Consider adding azelastine to reduce nasal congestion; Schedule follow-up appointment in 2 months to reassess symptoms
plan3: Refer to sleep specialist for further testing and evaluation; Encourage nocturnal CPAP use based on patient education and counseling; Schedule follow-up appointment in 3-6 months to reassess symptoms

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: decompensated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
plan1: Evaluate for volume overload/edema responsiveness with fluid restriction (1-2L/day) and ACEi/ARB optimization or add loop diuretic (e.g., metolazone 2.5 mg+furosemide 20 mg daily) if symptoms persist; Implement heart failure monitoring: weight (q4h for 48h, daily) and daily symptoms evaluation; consider ambulatory BP monitoring; Recheck diuretic response in 3–5 days and reassess for NYHA classification escalation (e.g., add IV isotropic infusion if hemodynamic instability detected)
plan2: Clarify myocardial ischemia suspicion via careful patient symptoms history (provocable dyspnea on exertion), monitor pulse rate at rest/with exertion, check nitroglycerin trial adherence/responsiveness; Order stress echocardiogram or ambulatory EKG monitoring (holter) if unconfirmed CAD likely; consider statin intensification if LDL remains elevated (>70 mg/dL); Assess beta-blocker compliance (bisoprolol 5 mg) and possible dose titration if dyspnea persists (monitor HR<60 or SBP<90)], or consider percutaneous revascularization if significant lesion detected
diagnosis3: acute respiratory exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
plan3: Assess COPD severity: FEV1/FVC ratio <70%, consider arterial blood gas if severe dyspnea/rales; check nebulizer compliance and add short-acting bronchodilator (e.g., ipratropium bromide via nebulizer) if symptoms worsening; Review inhaler technique and consider switching to particle-reducing medication, add inhaled corticosteroid (e.g., fluticasone 100mg BDP) if prior exacerbations >3x/year; Initiate patient education on pneumococcal booster if not up-to-date (evidence for COPD infections) and repeat AUDIT-C score for alcohol-related harm

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Obtain echocardiogram to evaluate cardiac function; Initiate diuretics to manage fluid overload; Consider BNP levels to assess heart failure severity
plan2: Order pulmonary function tests to assess lung function; Review inhaler technique and optimize bronchodilator therapy; Encourage smoking cessation support if applicable
plan3: Review current medication regimen for optimization; Monitor heart rate and blood pressure at each visit; Consider stress testing to evaluate for induced ischemia

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram; BNP Level; Diuretic (e.g., Furosemide)
plan2: ECG; Continue Aspirin and Atorvastatin; Consider further cardiac stress test
plan3: Assess for nasal congestion and inflammation; Consider topical nasal steroid treatment; Follow up with ENT specialist

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: ECG; Chest X-ray; Echocardiogram
plan2: Spirometry; Pulmonary Function Tests
plan3: Blood Tests; D-dimer

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: Decompensated Heart Failure with Left Heart Failure
plan1: Immediate outpatient echocardiogram to evaluate cardiac function and ventricular dysfunction; Urgent chest X-ray to identify signs of pulmonary edema or congestion; Initiate or reevaluate diuretic dose (e.g., adjust bisoprolol or loop diuretic if added for fluid overload)
plan2: Confirm or reassess home nebulizer access, adjust frequency if dyspnea persists; Review recent medication regimen for appropriate bronchodilator/inhaled cortisone use (evaluate for missed doses in acute flare); Consider spirometry if not up to date for pulmonary function assessment
diagnosis3: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) check and peripheral arterial disease considerations (if severe edema post-leg elevation but non-vascular source suspected)
plan3: Percutaneous ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement to rule out peripheral arterial disease contributing to edema; Monitor for claudication or rest pain as indirect symptom; Prescribe compression stockings if feasible for ambulatory use (to reduce stasis edema), avoid tight clothing/belongings

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: obtain chest X-ray to assess for fluid overload; start diuretics for edema management; schedule echocardiogram to evaluate cardiac function
plan2: conduct pulmonary function tests to assess lung capacity; prescribe inhaled bronchodilators as needed; review smoking cessation support resources
plan3: review current medications for optimization; monitor blood pressure and heart rate regularly; consider further cardiac evaluation with ECG

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram; BNP Level; Diuretics
plan2: Nasal Steroid; Saline Nasal Irrigation; Consider Antibiotics if Acute Symptoms
plan3: Continue Current Medications; Stress Management Techniques; Cardiac Rehabilitation Referral

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Diuretics (e.g., furosemide) for fluid overload and edema; ACE Inhibitors for heart failure management and to improve symptoms; ECG to assess for ischemic changes or arrhythmias
plan2: Inhaled Bronchodilators to relieve bronchospasm and improve airflow; Chest X-ray to check for lung pathology and confirm suspicion; Spirometry to assess lung function and confirm COPD
plan3: CT Pulmonary Angiography to evaluate lung vessels; Anticoagulants if pulmonary embolism diagnosed; Echocardiogram to evaluate cardiac function and structure

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Obtain urgent echocardiography to assess LVEF, wall motion abnormalities, and HF presentation; Order chest X-ray and BNP level to confirm fluid overload and cardiac etiology; Begin loop diuretic (e.g., furosemide) at recommended dose while monitoring for response to fluid volume reduction
diagnosis2: pulmonary hypertension or chronic restrictive pulmonary physiology
plan2: Pulmonary function testing (spirometry and 6-minute walk test) to evaluate restrictive/reversible airway contribution; Assess history for chronic cardiogenic risk factors and consider echocardiogram to exclude underlying restrictive LV function; Consider inhaled vasodilator stress test if clinical suspicion persists
diagnosis3: acute stress/psychosocial anxiety/depression (less likely given PHQ-2=0, DAST-10=2)
plan3: Reassess depression history/recognition despite PHQ-2=0 (screening tool limitations), consider re-evaluate AUDIT-C/ADHS symptoms

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Initiate diuretic therapy to manage edema and fluid overload; Schedule echocardiogram to assess heart function; Monitor electrolyte levels and renal function regularly
plan2: Optimize bronchodilator therapy with assessment of inhaler technique; Schedule pulmonary rehabilitation program; Consider oxygen therapy if hypoxemia is present
plan3: Continue pain management with NSAIDs as needed; Encourage low-impact exercise and physical therapy; Evaluate for assistive devices to improve mobility and reduce strain

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: ECG to assess for arrhythmias; BNP level to quantify cardiac strain; Assess fluid status and consider diuretics
plan2: Increase inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators; Oxygen therapy to maintain SpO2 > 90%; Consider antibiotics if purulent sputum
plan3: Assess for suicidal ideation; Referral to mental health professional for evaluation and support; Continue current anxiolytic medications

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Repeat spirometry in 6 months to assess for disease progression; Consider adding a mucolytic agent as adjunct therapy to bronchodilators; Advise on lifestyle modifications to optimize lung function (e.g., smoking cessation, exercise, weight management)
diagnosis2: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
plan2: Echocardiography or cardiac MRI to evaluate left ventricular function and assess for signs of heart failure; Consider changing patient's diuretic regimen or adding a beta-blocker as pharmacologic therapy; Increased monitoring for signs of exacerbation or worsening of heart failure (e.g., worsening edema, decreased exercise tolerance)
plan3: Upper endoscopy or colonoscopy to investigate sources of gastrointestinal bleeding or potential malignancy; Consider changing patient's pain management regimen or adding a proton pump inhibitor as adjunct therapy; Escalate patient's hospitalization status or admit to a specialized facility for further evaluation and management

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Repeat BNP or NT-proBNP for confirmation; start low-dose furosemide 20 mg daily; Optimize inhaler technique for albuterol and evaluate use of long-acting bronchodilator if FEV1/FVC persistently low; Review and target BP to <130/80 via lifestyle adjustments and consider ACE-I if no contraindications
plan2: Monitor oxygen saturation with pulse oximetry and consider non-invasive ventilation if hypoxia or respiratory failure worsens; Increase maintenance bronchodilators (salmeterol → long-acting beta-agonist like vilanterol or formoterol); Check spirometry at next visit to re-assess FEV1/FVC and consider pulmonary rehab

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
plan1: Increase fluticasone/salmeterol dosage if symptoms worsen; Consider systemic corticosteroids for acute exacerbation; Schedule follow-up spirometry in 1 month to monitor lung function
plan2: Evaluate for volume overload with weight monitoring; Consider diuretics for edema management; Request an echocardiogram to assess cardiac function
plan3: Monitor mental health symptoms closely; Consider referral for counseling or therapy; Reassess PHQ-2 score at the next visit

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Initiate diuretic therapy (e.g., furosemide); Assess ejection fraction and BNP levels; Optimize oxygen therapy and consider non-invasive ventilation
plan2: Administer bronchodilators (e.g., albuterol, ipratropium); Consider systemic corticosteroids; Monitor respiratory status and oxygen saturation
plan3: Continue current analgesics (naproxen); Consider referral to physical therapy; Assess for pain impacting mobility and quality of life

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Oxygen therapy; Salbutamol inhalation; Dexamethasone oral dose
plan2: Tobacco cessation therapy; Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol dry powder inhaler adjustment; Regular spirometry monitoring

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: pulmonary heart disease/volume overload (due to COPD with orthopnea/edematous signs)
plan1: Review/optimize sputum cultures or repeat chest X-ray if no baseline available (e.g., if worsening dyspnea in context of COPD exacerbation); Assess diuretic use (e.g., furosemide 20-40 mg PO/IV if no contraindications), consult vascular access specialist for adequate IV hydration if oral non-compliant; Re-evaluate hospice plan focus from cardiac/supportive care for symptom relief
diagnosis2: diastolic HF with secondary COPD-related volume overload
plan2: Monitor fluid restriction (1200-1500 ml/day) and follow-up on CHF assessment via telehealth/routine clinic visit in 3–4 weeks; Consider spot urines (e.g., daily weights + labs) for electrolyte/renal monitoring; elevate Na intake to ≤2 mEq/L if orthohydroses suspected; Evaluate O₂ saturation if hypoxia worsens or respiratory failure risk increases (e.g., via nasal Prongs/ECFMO support at 2L if not improving with medical mgmt)
diagnosis3: late-stage COPD with right heart strain/electrolyte imbalance
plan3: Review Albuterol dosing intensity/intervals (e.g., PRN MDI vs spacer) with pulmonary rehabilitation focus; optimize SAMLA taper if active flare; Hospice transition support (palliative care team input for respiratory distress/opioid co-prescibing adjuncts, e.g., benzos + gabapentin for anxiety); ensure comfort pain management review; Screen for dysphagia (e.g., modified barium swallow) if dietary tolerance decline noted per stress/fear history of assaultive environments

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Increase bronchodilator use as needed for dyspnea; Consider pulmonary rehabilitation program; Schedule a follow-up spirometry test
plan2: Order echocardiogram to assess cardiac function; Consider B-type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) test; Evaluate fluid management and adjust diuretics if edema persists
plan3: Review pain management options; Encourage low-impact exercises to improve mobility; Assess need for physical therapy evaluation

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: BNP level; Echocardiogram; Review medications
plan2: Albuterol and Ipratropium; Consider Antibiotics if infection suspected; Pulmonary Rehabilitation referral
plan3: Pain Management (Naproxen); Physical Therapy for mobility; Assess for secondary respiratory distress

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Order echocardiogram to assess cardiac function; Prescribe diuretics to manage fluid overload; Refer to Cardiology clinic for further evaluation
plan2: Administer antibiotics for suspected bacterial infection; Prescribe bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids for symptom control; Schedule follow-up spirometry to monitor lung function

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Obtain immediate transthoracic echocardiogram to assess left ventricular function, EF, and wall motion abnormalities; confirm diastolic dysfunction or fluid overload; Perform B-type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) testing to quantify cardiac stress markers; target BNP > 400 pg/mL likely in advanced HF; Assess and adjust diuretic therapy or hydralazine/isosorbide mononitrate if congestive symptoms persist or worsen; remeasure daily weight and edema progression
diagnosis3: hypothenar hammer syndrome-related muscle weakness contributing to pulmonary deconditioning/pneumonia risk
plan3: Re-evaluate orthotic management for osteoarthritis knee support and assess balance; introduce mobility modifications to prevent falls and pressure injury; Consider nutritional assessment to address possible calorie deficit from reduced food intake secondary to chronic pain/edema; discuss appetite stimulants or enteral tube if needed; Provide stress-informed pulmonary hygiene education, including upright positioning to reduce edema pooling, and remindance of daily decongestive therapy for arthritis flare-ups during exacerbations

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: obtain echocardiogram to assess heart function; consider BNP test to evaluate heart failure; initiate diuretics for fluid management
plan2: continue bronchodilator therapy with albuterol; consider systemic corticosteroids for exacerbation; schedule follow-up spirometry to monitor lung function
plan3: provide counseling resources for stress management; evaluate for potential psychiatric referral; monitor PHQ-2 scores at follow-up visits

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Spirometry with bronchodilator challenge; Continue fluticasone propionate/salmeterol dry powder inhaler and albuterol inhalation solution; Pulmonary rehabilitation referral
plan2: BNP test; Echocardiogram; Review current medications and adjust as needed
plan3: Pain management with naproxen sodium; Physical therapy referral for mobility training; Assess impact of pain on breathing

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol dry powder inhaler adjustment; Oxygen therapy initiation; Regular exercise program initiation
plan2: Echocardiogram for cardiac causes evaluation; Oxygen therapy adjustment; Fluid status reassessment

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Cardiovascular stress testing (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: hospital-acquired volume overload/potential heart failure exacerbation
plan1: Evaluate with echocardiogram to assess LV function/ejection fraction; Serum BNP/BNP level to exclude cardiac cause of edema/dyspnea; Assess fluid status: weigh, diuretic trial, daily vital checks for weight change/refill urgency
diagnosis2: unstable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation
plan2: Repeat FEV1/FVC and consider sputum culture/bacterial toxin panel if rales/albuterol inefficacy noted; Review bronchodilator use (add long-acting options) and consider inhaled corticosteroid optimization; Consider short-acting oxygen therapy monitoring saturations <90% or SpO₂ trends
plan3: Check lab for anion gap if new decompensation, consider VDRL/Vitamins B1/B12 if malnutrition secondary to oral meds; Assess for respiratory tract infection (sinus culture if persistent symptoms post sinusitis prior to hospice), evaluate nutritional status; Pulmonary toileting measures if compromised mobility (physiotherapy, assistive positioning if edema prominent)

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Assess electrolytes and renal function; Initiate diuretics if volume overload confirmed; Evaluate need for echocardiography to assess cardiac function
plan2: Monitor renal function with regular serum creatinine; Optimize management of diabetes and hypertension; Consider referral to nephrology for ongoing management
plan3: Review and adjust diabetes management plan; Check HbA1c regularly; Evaluate for possible diabetic neuropathy progression

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction and valve function; Continuous cardiac monitoring with Holter monitor to assess arrhythmia; Optimize diuretic therapy (furosemide) based on fluid status
plan2: Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR) monitoring every 3 months; Assess phosphate and Vitamin D levels; Continue low-protein diet as tolerated
plan3: Adjust metformin dosage based on glucose monitoring; Review and potentially add SGLT2 inhibitor for glycemic control and renal protection; Regular foot exams to screen for neuropathy and ulceration

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Renal ultrasound to assess kidney function and structure; Lifestyle changes including reduced salt intake, fluid restriction, and exercise; Ongoing monitoring of serum creatinine and electrolytes
diagnosis2: Chronic Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
plan2: Cardiac evaluation including echocardiogram and stress test; Adjusting medications including beta-blockers and ACE inhibitors; Monitoring of symptoms, ejection fraction, and exercise tolerance
diagnosis3: Respiratory Congestion due to Heart Failure and Diabetic Nephropathy
plan3: Hospital admission for oxygen therapy and diuretics, pulmonary toilet if necessary; Invasive respiratory support if severe; Monitoring of respiratory status and oxygen saturation

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: volume overload/heart failure exacerbated by CKD Stage 1/renal dysfunction (HF with reduced EF likely)
plan1: Consider repeat echocardiogram to evaluate EF and assess hemodynamics; document LV ejection fraction (EF) if not updated in years.; Monitor for worsening edema/orthopnea and escalate home care (eg, diuretic titration with 24-hour urine output monitoring); Evaluate for non-pharmacologic interventions (e.g., bodyweight monitoring, daily fluid intake/record review)
diagnosis2: respiratory muscle fatigue/chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (exertional dyspnea/orthopnea)
plan2: Pulmonary rehabilitation referral focusing on exercise tolerance, breathing techniques, and pulmonary hydration.; Bronchorespiratory exercises with humidified air if breath sounds (rales) persistent post-reversal/fluids.; Tobacco cessation reinforcement (already confirmed non-smoker, but reemphasis on systemic health triggers respiratory decline)
diagnosis3: hypercoagulable state/repeated ischemic events (clopidogrel insufficient effect on residual CAD risk)
plan3: Reassess antiplatelet duration: add or transition to prasugrel/clopidogrel triple therapy with P2Y12 testing (if tolerated).; Consider stress echo with Dobutamine if EF <40% at reassessment, despite prior bypass surgery.; Optimize blood pressure (<130/80): titrate amlodipine/lisinopril maximally allowed on chronic CKD (e.g., reduce lisinopril dose if GFR <50).

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Evaluate for potential heart failure through echocardiogram; Manage fluid retention with diuretics; Optimize heart rate and BP control with current medications
plan2: Monitor kidney function with regular serum creatinine and GFR tests; Assess proteinuria with a repeat urinalysis; Consider nephrology referral for management of diabetes-related kidney disorder
plan3: Check complete blood count (CBC) to assess hemoglobin levels; Evaluate iron studies for potential iron deficiency; Consider supplementation based on results and review medication interactions

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
plan1: Echocardiogram to assess ejection fraction and cardiac function; Initiate or optimize guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, including ACE inhibitor or ARNI, beta-blocker, and diuretic; Monitor for signs and symptoms of fluid overload and adjust diuretic regimen as needed
plan2: Renal ultrasound to evaluate kidney size and structure; Monitor serum creatinine and eGFR to assess progression of CKD; Dietary modification - low protein, potassium, and phosphorus diet
diagnosis3: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Diabetic Neuropathy
plan3: HbA1c monitoring every 3-6 months; Optimize blood glucose control with metformin, considering additional agents if needed; Foot examination and education regarding diabetic foot care

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
plan1: Repeat urinalysis and blood tests to assess kidney function; Adjust medication regimen to minimize nephrotoxic effects; Consider initiating pharmacologic treatment for CKD with an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor or an angiotensin receptor-neuronal blocker (ARNB) if evidence of proteinuria or hematuria is present

plan1: Review/confirm diagnosis via structured proteinuria-to-creative clearance (detailed urine collection for 24h or targeted protein/g creatinine) or eGFR tracking trend for progression; Suspend lisinopril pending GFR stability/refractory edema; reconsider ACEi initiation if edema improves or GFR stabilizes but consult nephrology urgently if BP uncontrolled (systolic ≥140) despite BP medication; Initiate diuretic (e.g., metolazone + furosemide) if orthopnea/edema persists while reassessing kidney function (target serial creatinine/BUN in 7–14 days)
diagnosis2: decompensated heart failure with left ventricular dysfunction
plan2: Echocardiogram ASAP to quantify LVEF/evaluate for systolic dysfunction/metrics; consider stress MPI if EF unclear or EF borderline without perfusion defects present; Refer urgently to interdisciplinary HF team ( cardiology + nephrology) for heart failure medication optimization (consider hydralazine/isosorbide dinitrate for symptomatic relief if ACEi/arb refractory); Monitor serum B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP > 100 pg/mL or NT-proBNP > 300 pg/mL); reconsider cardiac MR imaging if volume overload/edema persists despite maximized ACEi/ARB + diuretics
diagnosis3: unmasked diabetic ketoacidosis with volume depletion
plan3: Confirm diagnosis via capillary/lipid levels (ketones) if glucosuria detected (non-insulin failure or missed doses); assess for non-renal causes (e.g., stress hyperadrenocorticism); Start intravenous normal saline (NS) for volume resuscitation if dehydration present (no hypotension + orthopnea/RALES); consider isotonic NaCl 3L/24h if rapid correction needed for normotensive patient; Reevaluate insulin initiation if anion gap elevated (ΔKetoinsulin) with worsening renal function; monitor electrolytes (K+ especially if insulin pending)

diagnosis3: Urine tract infection/inflammation (e.g., pyelonephritis/acute pyclonephritis) complicating CKD/nephropathy
plan3: Obtain urine culture with Gram stain immediately; consider IV antibiotics (e.g., ceftriaxone + fluoroquinolone) if clinical decompensation. Hydrate aggressively and reexamine serum electrolytes. Review antimicrobial stewardship (e.g., culture-guided prescribing).

diagnosis1: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
plan1: Echocardiography to assess LV systolic/diastolic function and fluid volume status, pulmonary artery occlusion pressure (PAOP). Measure N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) ≥7000 pg/mL (elevated suggests CHF).; Diuretic titration (e.g., furosemide dose adjustment with monitoring), ensure strict sodium restriction <2 g/day. Review HFpEF-focused medications: dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers if contraindicated.; Fluoroscopy-guided intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) for assessment if echo inconclusive or hemodynamic instability, consider pulmonary artery catheterization if uncertainty remains.
diagnosis2: Chronic pulmonary restrictive disease or left atrial/myocardial compromise
plan2: High-resolution chest CT to evaluate for restrictive lung physiology/atelectasis/emphysema/posterior mediastinal mass. Consider assessment for restrictive ventilatory pattern if O2 use/symptom worsening (low FEV1/FVC).; Cardiac-focused pulmonary physiologic investigation (e.g., sleep study if orthopnea nocturnal polyuria reported, or if respiratory insufficiency at rest). Ensure pulmonary hygiene with inhaled bronchodilators if reversible component suspected.; Consider transthoracic echocardiogram if suspicion elevates for underlying diastolic dysfunction or LVM.
diagnosis3: Diaphragm palsy/compressive neuropathies (C5-C6) or neuromuscular restrictive process
plan3: Neurologic referral for Vitalscan evaluation/Touchlight, consider EMG/Nerve Conduction Study to identify neuropathy/compressive pathology. Monitor vital capacity (VC) trends for respiratory failure risk.; Neuromusculoskeletal evaluation for structural compressive lesion (e.g., T1/T2 imaging for posterior cervical spine assessment). Consider functional exercise to assess diaphragmatic function (coughing, splinting).; If ataxia/floppiness prominent: respiratory hygiene protocol including incentive spirometry, daily Pneucheck 3D, manual assisted ventilation if profound weakness.

plan1: Order BNP/NT-proBNP serum test to confirm diagnosis and assess severity; Perform transthoracic echocardiography to confirm EF, assess LV dysfunction, and rule out cardiomyopathies; Observe blood pressure and monitor edema progression for diuretic initiation if congestion exacerbates
diagnosis2: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy (LVH) secondary to ischemic heart disease
plan2: Monitor metoprolol adherence and consider beta-blockade optimization to mitigate HF risk; Review stress management interventions despite mild/none stress symptoms; Plan for stress echocardiogram if symptoms worsen or new ECG changes occur
plan3: Review clopidogrel dose adjustments if bleeding risk is present with diuretic initiation; Assess lab refill adherence (simvastatin) for lipid management to prevent CV event recurrence; Consider salt restriction education to mitigate peripheral edema risk

plan1: Order echocardiogram to assess cardiac function; Initiate diuretics to manage fluid retention; Check BNP levels to evaluate heart failure severity
plan2: Perform chest X-ray to check for pulmonary congestion; Monitor respiratory status and oxygen saturation; Educate on lifestyle modifications for symptom management
plan3: Schedule follow-up colonoscopy to monitor the colon polyp; Educate on dietary changes to reduce cancer risk; Consider referral to gastroenterology for ongoing surveillance

plan_label: Electrocardiographic procedure (procedure); Assessment using New York Heart Association Classification (procedure)
diagnosis1: Heart Failure (HF with preserved Ejection Fraction or HFpEF)
plan1: BNP/NT-proBNP level at baseline, confirmatory echocardiogram (assess LVEF and diastolic function); Pulmonary edema ruling with chest X-ray: review for pulmonary congestion and hydrothorax
plan2: Coronary angiography to monitor lesion progression/revascularization, if not already done in 8 years; Monitor metabolic stress (e.g., GAD-7/PHQ-2 consistency) vs. HF-related emotional impact if mood is suspected to worsen symptoms
diagnosis3: Mild Pulmonary Dysfunction or Early Obstructive Lung Disease
plan3: High-resolution pulmonary functional testing (spirometry with reversibility testing if COPD suspected); Lung sound auscultation for persistent rales: document pattern as short-term follow-up to exclude early restrictive/obstructive pattern changes
